style: 90s industrial shock-rock music video crossed with early-2000s post-hardcore: 16mm film grain, bleach-bypass contrast, crushed blacks, hard white strobes, cold blue fluorescent and red alarm light, a grimy low-ceilinged basement show with exposed pipes. Dark, creepy, theatrical techno-horror. The four porcelain lobster androids keep the same faces, antennae, claws and torn black stage clothes: white singer with long black hair and black oil tears, black-porcelain guitarist, blood-red bassist, bone-coloured drummer. No text, no lip-sync, no talking.

shots.prompt: Dynamic handheld wide shot of the whole band exploding into the song: the white singer screams with its head thrown back, the guitarist and bassist headbang violently in unison, the drummer pounds the kit, the crowd of kids in black hoodies slam into each other in a mosh pit in the foreground. Hard white strobes flash, the bare fluorescent tube flickers.

The handheld camera rushes forward through the crowd to a tight close-up of the white porcelain singer screaming, long black hair whipping around its face as it thrashes, black oil tears streaking down the porcelain cheeks, claw gripping the microphone stand. Strobes, sweat and haze.

Low-angle camera down among the crowd: the human emo kids in black hoodies slam dance and crash into each other, fists swinging, hair flying, bodies colliding in the mosh pit, the porcelain band thrashing behind them in strobe light. Chaotic, shaky, energetic.

The camera pushes in on the blood-red porcelain bassist on the right as it keeps playing: its left arm unravels into long streams of glowing white digits, 0.0000 0.0000, peeling off and drifting into the air like ash. Continuous on-camera transformation with no cuts. The rest of the band keeps thrashing.

The blood-red porcelain bassist keeps playing hard and headbanging while its body keeps coming apart, streams of glowing digits pouring off its arm and shoulder and blowing away into the dark. Handheld camera circles it slowly, strobes flashing.

The kids in the crowd stand completely still with blank faces, lit from below by the phones they hold up, filming. Nobody dances. Only their phones move slightly. Slow, creepy push in. Behind them the band flickers in and out as numbers.

The bone-coloured porcelain drummer keeps drumming furiously, sticks blurring, while its body dissolves further into a glowing field of small arrows that all flow downhill like a gradient field. Red light pulses with each hit. Handheld camera, slight shake.

The black-porcelain guitarist slowly raises its cracked hand toward its face and stares at it in horror as glowing numbers drip from the crack like blood onto the guitar strings. Its head trembles. Slow push in, strobe flicker, creepy and theatrical.

The camera pushes in on the bone-coloured drummer in the middle as it keeps drumming: its arms and chest dissolve into a glowing field of arrows that stream downhill and scatter. Continuous on-camera transformation with no cuts. The singer and guitarists keep headbanging in front.

Slow-motion: the whole band headbangs in unison, hair and antennae swinging in long arcs, while glowing digits drift off their half-dissolved bodies like embers. The crowd's fists rise slowly. Strobes freeze the motion. Handheld camera drifts sideways.

The white porcelain singer screams with its chest ripped open, thrashing its head, porcelain shards falling from the hole. Inside the chest the floating matrix of glowing numbers spins slowly and is otherwise completely empty. Low angle, hard strobes.
Very slow push in past the blank faces toward the glowing phone screens held up in the dark, the kids motionless as statues, screen light flickering on their faces. Eerie, voyeuristic, almost still.

Half-time breakdown in slow motion: the stage lights die to a single shaft of white light from above. The band headbangs slowly and heavily, the guitarist and bassist swinging their whole bodies down on each crushing chord, the crowd pit opening up. Locked-off wide camera, haze in the light.

Close on the black-porcelain guitarist's hand on the guitar: glowing numbers drip from the crack in its palm onto the strings and body of the guitar, pooling and running down the frets as it keeps playing, its head bowed. Slow, heavy, red light.

Locked-off, almost still: the single clear tear slowly runs down the intact porcelain cheek, catching the only light, while the dissolved half of the face drifts away in soft glowing digits. Total quiet, the hair barely moving.

The tear on the porcelain cheek evaporates into drifting decimal digits, and then the rest of the face slowly follows, crumbling into floating glowing numbers that drift off into darkness. Continuous on-camera transformation with no cuts. Static camera.

The server room burns, flames roaring up the racks, sparks raining down. The half-dissolved white singer screams and thrashes at center, the band behind it headbanging as streams of digits, still playing. Red strobes and orange firelight, handheld camera shaking.

The empty basement stage: the wireframe guitar, bass and drum kit play themselves, strings vibrating and cymbals shaking with nobody there, grid lines flickering. The bare bulb swings slowly. Static wide camera, haze, eerie and silent.
